metadata.notes: Documentation describes password authentication via flows/stages, not a REST login API. This operation represents initiating the web login flow required before password submission.
Docs describe browser logout URL, not explicit admin token revocation API for sessions in supplied material

enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

metadata.documented_via: resource lifecycle implied by create/edit/delete UI patterns; exact endpoint details not provided in supplied docs

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: SAML sources can be configured to allow IdP-initiated logins, and the docs warn this may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified.
saml.note: Acceptance of IdP-initiated login under this setting is by design and should not be flagged as a flow-coherence bug.

saml.description: When a Source stage suspends a flow and the configured resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning on return.
saml.note: A restarted flow after timeout is expected behavior, not session confusion.

saml.description: Source-stage embedded source flows must not contain a User Login stage, otherwise the nested flow authenticates directly instead of resuming the original flow.
saml.note: Unexpected direct authentication in this configuration is by design.

saml.description: Using email address as SAML NameID is discouraged because users are generally free to change email addresses.
saml.note: Identity drift or relinking under email-based NameID may be an expected consequence of mutable identifiers.

saml.description: Different SAML NameID policies intentionally produce different identifier forms such as hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, session ID, or email.
saml.note: Do not compare identities across different NameID policy settings as if they should remain byte-identical.

saml.description: Transient SAML NameID values are based on the user's session ID.
saml.note: Different NameID values across logins are expected and should not be flagged as identity instability.

saml.description: A valid unexpired bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls.
saml.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by OAuth2/OIDC token usage docs
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer-token reuse as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: The nbf claim is optional and lack of enforcement is spec-compliant.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf as a vulnerability solely on that basis.

saml.description: When an administrator reconfigures trust anchors, issuers, or signing keys, acceptance under the new configuration is expected.
saml.note: Do not flag logins that succeed because an admin intentionally changed trusted configuration.

saml.description: SAML sources can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation warns this may be a security risk because the request is not verified.
saml.note: If enabled by admin, acceptance of IdP-initiated login is configuration-driven and should not be treated as an implementation bug by itself.

saml.description: An administrator can reconfigure SAML/OIDC trust settings and the new configuration taking effect is by design.
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication under newly admin-authorized trust settings as trust-anchor substitution.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML source/provider configuration and flows take effect as part of normal configuration-driven behavior.
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication under newly authorized configuration as a trust-anchor or coherence violation.

saml.description: Applications are accessible to all users when no bindings are defined.
saml.note: Authorization tests must add bindings/policies first; otherwise broad access is expected.

saml.constraint: SAML testing against authentik as SP MUST use the SAML Source ACS endpoint /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/. The SAML provider endpoints under /application/saml/{application_slug}/... are authentik acting as IdP for downstream applications, not the upstream SAML-consumption path.

For I1 signature-validation tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure the SAML source to require signed assertions/requests if such options exist in the source configuration. The docs only state that SAML Source supports signed requests; they do not state secure-by-default verification semantics. A success under permissive/default source settings may reflect configuration, not a proof-integrity bug.

For I1 issuer-validation tests (saml_issuer_mismatch), the fuzzer MUST configure the SAML source with the expected IdP issuer/entity ID from metadata and then send a mismatched Issuer. If issuer/entity ID is left loosely configured or inferred from imported metadata without verification, acceptance may be a setup artifact rather than an issuer-validation flaw.

For I2 replay and expiry tests on SAML assertions (saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_expired_assertion), the sequence MUST include a control SAML login against the same source configuration first. Without a control, rejection of the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from a broken source/flow configuration.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving external SAML authentication embedded via Source stage, the fuzzer MUST account for Source stage resume timeout. If the suspended flow exceeds the configured resume timeout, authentik restarts the flow from the beginning by design; this is not a coherence violation.

For I3 tests involving Source stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. The docs state this prevents resuming the original flow and directly authenticates the pending user instead, which would invalidate atomicity/coherence test assumptions.

For I3 admin-change sequences, remember that authentik evaluates some policies dynamically at stage run time by default, but stage bindings can be configured to Evaluate when flow is planned. A valid coherence test must hold this setting constant; differences caused by plan-time vs run-time policy evaluation are configuration effects, not stale-session bugs.

For I4 principal-binding tests on SAML, the fuzzer MUST vary both NameID and mapped attributes such as email/username because authentik supports configurable property mappings and NameID mapping. Identity binding may depend on source mappings rather than raw NameID alone; testing only NameID can misattribute mapping-driven linking behavior.

For I4 email-binding collision tests, avoid treating email-based NameID as a safe stable identifier. The docs explicitly warn that users are generally free to change email addresses and recommend avoiding email as NameID or disallowing email changes. Collisions or relinking under email-based NameID may be configuration-induced.

For I4 unverified-email-account-linking tests, note that authentik's OAuth/OIDC docs state email_verified defaults to False as of 2025.10 because authentik lacks an authoritative verification source. If a custom mapping forces email_verified=True, linking outcomes reflect admin mapping policy; keep this constant when comparing behaviors.

For I5 SAML authorization-binding tests, property mappings control which attributes are emitted to downstream applications. The fuzzer MUST keep provider/source property mappings fixed across baseline and attack cases; changes in granted attributes caused by mapping edits are by design and not authorization escalation.

The OAuth/OIDC UserInfo endpoint is /application/o/userinfo/, token endpoint is /application/o/token/, revocation endpoint is /application/o/revoke/, and introspection endpoint is /application/o/introspect/. If the SAML test harness relies on bearer-token verification after SAML login, it must obtain an OAuth access token separately; a raw SAML login to authentik's SAML source does not itself document an API bearer token response.

For SAML MFA-bypass testing, authentik flow behavior is stage-driven. A valid test must compare the same user under a password flow that includes Authenticator Validation/User Login stages versus a SAML source path or Source-stage path that omits equivalent MFA enforcement. Differences caused by intentionally different flows are configuration issues, not necessarily bypasses.

SAML login testing against authentik as SP MUST use the SAML source ACS endpoint /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with HTTP POST form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState. The executor MUST initiate the SP flow first so the forged response carries the correct InResponseTo value.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, create the SAML source with default settings and do NOT add extra verification hardening beyond the configured verification certificate behavior. Then submit the forged SAMLResponse via saml_login. This distinguishes insecure defaults from explicit admin hardening.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, configure the SAML source with an expected upstream issuer/entity ID. If issuer/entity ID is left unset, issuer comparison may be skipped by configuration and a successful login is not evidence of a signature-validation flaw.

Allow IDP-Initiated Logins on a SAML source is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For security testing, keep allow_idp_initiated disabled unless the specific test is intentionally measuring IdP-initiated acceptance behavior.

For I2 replay tests on SAML assertions, include a control login with a fresh valid assertion before the replayed or expired assertion. Without a control, rejection may reflect broken source configuration rather than freshness enforcement.
For I2 saml_expired_assertion, send a control assertion first, then an assertion with NotOnOrAfter in the past. A failed expired assertion without a successful control is inconclusive.

For I2 saml_one_time_use_replay and saml_assertion_id_replay, reuse the exact same Assertion/@ID across both saml_login events. Changing any assertion identifier turns the sequence into two independent logins and cannot test replay detection.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving external sources embedded in flows, source authentication/enrollment flows used by a Source stage MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. Documentation states this prevents resuming the original flow and instead directly authenticates the pending user, which would invalidate atomicity/coherence conclusions.

For I3 config-change sequences, authentik flow planning can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test must account for this documented behavior and must not flag by-design differences caused solely by stage-binding evaluation mode.

For I3 SAML MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, compare the same user through password flow versus SAML source flow only after confirming the password flow actually reaches MFA challenge. If the password flow is not configured to require MFA, SAML success without MFA is not evidence of bypass.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier authentik receives. Persistent may map to a hashed ID, transient to session ID, and emailAddress to email. Keep NameID policy fixed across compared test cases or identity differences are by configuration, not collisions.

Email-based NameID is documented as mutable because users may change email addresses. Do NOT treat account changes caused by an admin- or user-changed email-based NameID as an automatic I4 collision; this is a documented risky configuration choice, not necessarily a broker parsing flaw.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, compare both NameID and email-derived linking behavior. Because authentik supports property mappings and source flows, the fuzzer must verify whether linking is based on email or another mapped identifier before concluding principal collapse.

For I5 saml_no_conditions and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, use the SAML source as SP and submit assertions omitting Conditions or AudienceRestriction. Success is only meaningful when the source is otherwise correctly configured and the ACS flow was initiated normally.

Application access in authentik is allow-all by default when no bindings are defined. For I5 authorization-binding tests, explicitly bind policies/groups/users to the application under test; otherwise successful access may simply reflect the documented default-open application behavior.

When no OAuth/OIDC scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. If verification uses OAuth userinfo or tokens after SAML-related setup, always request explicit minimal scopes to avoid false I5 positives from default broad scope behavior.

SAML Single Logout back-channel requires POST SLS binding. Do not interpret absence of back-channel logout under Redirect binding as a session-management flaw; the documentation states back-channel is unsupported for Redirect binding.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, the SAML source configuration MUST set the IdP Issuer/Entity ID. The docs describe this field as the identifier for the SAML IdP and note it is used to identify the SP on the IdP side. If the source is created without a concrete expected issuer/entity ID, an issuer-mismatch test can pass trivially because there is no configured issuer to compare against.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, configure the SAML source with a concrete SP Issuer/Entity ID and use the documented ACS URL https://<authentik>/source/saml/<source-slug>/acs/. Audience tests are only meaningful when the SP identity is fixed; otherwise acceptance may reflect missing audience configuration rather than a validation flaw.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion testing, include a CONTROL login using the same SAML source and a non-expired assertion before sending expired_assertion=true. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from a broken SAML source setup, bad ACS target, or unrelated flow failure.

For I2 replay tests against SAML assertions, use the SAME Assertion/@ID across both saml_login events when testing assertion replay or OneTimeUse replay. The docs identify the ACS endpoint as the assertion consumer and describe SAML assertions as the consumed artifact; replay testing is only valid if the exact same assertion identifier is reused.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving external SAML authentication, do NOT treat legitimate admin configuration changes as vulnerabilities. The docs state flows, stages, and bindings are evaluated dynamically and can change behavior based on current configuration. A valid I3 test must show inconsistent handling of the SAME request or suspended flow state, not merely that a new login follows updated admin configuration.

For I3 suspended-flow tests involving the Source stage, account for the documented Resume timeout. If the suspended flow exceeds this timeout, authentik restarts the flow from the beginning on return from the source. Do NOT flag this restart as a coherence bug unless the timeout was not exceeded.

For I3 source-stage tests, the source's authentication and enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. The docs explicitly warn that if a User Login stage is bound in the source flow, the original flow will not resume and the pending user will be authenticated directly. Failing to respect this causes false positives that look like flow hijacking or broken session binding.

For I3 SAML MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, verify the baseline password flow actually challenges for MFA before attempting SAML login. authentik flow behavior is stage- and policy-driven, and MFA may be skipped depending on stage bindings, last-validation threshold, or passkey policies. Without a baseline MFA challenge, successful SAML login without MFA is not evidence of bypass.

For I4 identity-binding tests on SAML, vary both NameID and mapped attributes such as email because authentik supports configurable NameID property mappings and multiple NameID policies. The docs state NameID can be mapped from different properties and may be persistent hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, or email address. A collision test that changes only one field may miss the actual binding key.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, avoid using Email-address NameID as the sole identifier unless the test intentionally targets email-based binding. The docs explicitly warn that email-based NameID is mutable by default and recommend avoiding it or preventing email changes. If email NameID is configured, account linking or identity merge by email may be by design configuration risk rather than parser confusion.

For I4 tests involving transient identifiers, do NOT use the Transient NameID policy when you need stable principal comparison across logins. The docs state transient NameID is based on the user's session ID, so repeated logins are expected to produce different identifiers by design.

For I4 tests involving persistent identifiers, prefer the Persistent NameID policy because the docs state it uses the user's hashed ID and should remain stable. This is the correct baseline for detecting unintended identity collapse or merge.

For I1/I5 tests of IdP-initiated login, note that the SAML source option Allow IDP-Initiated Logins may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified, per the docs. Acceptance of an unsolicited IdP-initiated response is BY CONFIGURATION and must not be conflated with failure to validate a request-bound InResponseTo in SP-initiated flows.

The SAML source ACS endpoint for authentik as SP is /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/. The fuzzer MUST post forged SAMLResponse values to this ACS path, not to the SAML provider IdP SSO endpoints under /application/saml/{application_slug}/..., which are for authentik acting as IdP.

SAML provider endpoints under /application/saml/{application_slug}/sso/... are IdP endpoints for applications authenticating against authentik. They are not the upstream-consumption endpoint for SAML source tests. Using them for saml_login would invert roles and invalidate all SAML-source security results.

The User Login stage Session duration parameter has sentinel semantics: seconds=0 means the authentik session expires when the browser is closed, not an immediate zero-second invalid session. Do not interpret 0 as 'already expired' in freshness tests.

The Authenticator Validation stage Last validation threshold has sentinel semantics: a non-zero value enables less-frequent MFA validation, while the default zero means validation is required every time. Do not assume 0 disables validation; it enforces validation on every execution.

The Email Authenticator Setup stage Token Expiration is documented in minutes with a default of 30. Freshness tests involving email-based MFA or email verification must account for this default lifetime rather than assuming single-use or near-immediate expiry.

The Email stage supports rate limiting via Account Recovery Max Attempts and Account Recovery Cache Timeout. If a test repeatedly triggers recovery or email verification flows, rate limiting can cause failures unrelated to the invariant under test. Reset or vary identities between attempts.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
